stances.claim: For the popular and the show biz, the defining event of the last Christmas season may have been the DongYan 'royal wedding' on December 30 at Immaculate Conception Cathedral in Cubao -- Dingdong Dantes and Marian Rivera, with PNoy as 'witness of honor,' 15 officiating clergy, 40 principal sponsors, and an extensive numerology of eight (8-second kiss, 2:38 PM ceremony, 800-seat cathedral, 6:08 PM reception, 18,000-seat MOA Arena)

CJ's own defining season event was the quiet dinner for 16 honoring Dr. Shoichiro Toyoda (89-year-old Toyota Motors honorary chair) hosted by Dr. George S.K. Ty -- ultra-significant not for menu or VIPs but for Dr. Ty's P1 billion donation to the Toyota School of Technology in Sta. Rosa, Laguna established in honor of Dr. Toyoda

Toyota Philippines is the only Toyota affiliate in the world in which the giant Japanese auto maker holds a minority interest (35%) while the local partner Metrobank group owns 51% (Mitsui 14%) -- and Toyota has dominated PH motoring for all 27 years of the Metrobank partnership, an unmatched continuous market-leadership record

CJ told Dr. Ty that by establishing TST in honor of Dr. Toyoda he was really performing a great service to our people because science and technology are essential to propel our country to sustainable prosperity -- and though established in honor of the Toyota leader, the school will remain in the Philippines

The second major season event was the inauguration of 23 new carillon bells donated by Alberto and Sylvia Lina to the Manila Cathedral -- prior 14 bells from 2011 were augmented by CJP's request (as Manila Cathedral Foundation president) for 9 more, to which Bert volunteered a complete new set of 23 from the Netherlands rather than risk tuning mismatch

Bert Lina explained the philosophy: 'To me, bells are the voice of God. When they ring, they call our faithful to worship in His church' -- and offered to donate the old 14 bells to a Yolanda-stricken diocese

Three significant books launched during the season of grace: (1) GMA Network chair Felipe G. 'Henry' Gozon's 'Autobiography' at his 75th birthday -- CJ had asked Henry in the late 1990s to join SC but he humbly declined for his TV-radio freedom-of-expression mission; CJ's earlier tribute calls him 'Gutsy with a capital G'; (2) Eduardo H. Yap's 'Stirred, Not Shaken' -- CJ foreword characterizes Eddie's '6Gs' (gift of gab, gift of giving, gift of genius); (3) Fr. Roberto B. Manansala's 'Echoes of God's Love' -- homilies for one whole liturgical year (Cycle B)

Brief mentions for the rest: lovely Christmas musicale at the home of Ave and Helen Cruz; Titoy Pardo's solemn affiliation to the De La Salle Brotherhood; 50th wedding anniversary of Louie and Triccie Sison; F. Sionil Jose's 90th birthday -- but let's not ever forget, the birth of our Lord Jesus Christ is the real reason for the joyous season

one_paragraph_summary: Panganiban delivers a year-in-review of his Christmas-season defining events. For the popular and the show biz, the defining event of the last Christmas season may have been the 'royal wedding' of DongYan -- Dingdong Dantes and Marian Rivera -- at the Immaculate Conception Cathedral in Cubao, Quezon City on December 30, with PNoy as 'witness of honor.' The star-studded nuptial was officiated by 15 men of the cloth (led by Cubao Bishop Honesto Ongtioco with a quotable homily by Bishop Ted Bacani), attended by 40 principal sponsors, 25 secondary sponsors, 18 groomsmen, 18 bridesmaids, 8 bridal showers, 2 marriage proposals and 500 security personnel, and sidelighted by the 'reconciliation' of Kris and Ai Ai. Eight was obviously the couple's favorite number -- evidenced by their 8-second kiss, exact ceremony time (2:38 PM) at the 800-seat Cubao Cathedral, and exact reception time (6:08 PM) at the 18,000-seat Mall of Asia Arena. Lesser mortals had their own momentous season events, perhaps not as grand and as eye-popping but momentous nonetheless. As for CJ, his season events were topped by a quiet dinner for 16 held in honor of Dr. Shoichiro Toyoda, the 89-year-old honorary chair of Toyota Motors of Japan, hosted by Dr. George S.K. Ty, group chair of the Metrobank conglomerate. What made the dinner ultra-significant was not the menu or the VIP attendees, but Dr. Ty's P1-billion donation to the Toyota School of Technology in Sta. Rosa, Laguna. Toyota Philippines is the only Toyota affiliate in the world in which the giant Japanese auto maker holds a minority interest (35 percent) while the local partner (Metrobank group) owns 51 percent (Mitsui and Co. holds the remaining 14 percent); elsewhere Toyota Japan always owns and controls the majority. Toyota has dominated the Philippine motoring industry consistently for all 27 years of partnership with Metrobank -- in no other country has the Japanese automotive giant topped the market continuously for such a long period. Dr. Ty said that, in gratitude, he thought of establishing the TST in honor of Dr. Toyoda, a direct descendant of Toyota founder Sakichi Toyoda. CJ replied that, in so doing, he was really performing a great service to our people because science and technology are essential to propel our country to sustainable prosperity; besides, though established in honor of the Toyota leader, the school will remain in the Philippines. The second major season event was the formal inauguration of the 23 new carillon bells donated by Alberto and Sylvia Lina to the Manila Cathedral. Prior to its recent refitting and renovation, the cathedral received 14 carillon bells from the Linas in 2011; but after CJ (as president of the Manila Cathedral Foundation) requested Bert to add nine more bells, Bert volunteered to order a complete new set of 23 bells from the Netherlands. Explained Bert: 'If I ordered nine new bells, they may not be in tune with the 14 existing. So, I will give a complete set of 23 new ones. After all, to me, bells are the voice of God. When they ring, they call our faithful to worship in His church.' What to do with the 'old' set of 14? 'Well,' Bert said, smiling, 'I can donate them to another church, perhaps in a Yolanda-stricken diocese.' Significant, too, were three books launched during the season of grace. (1) The 'Autobiography' of GMA Network chair and CEO Felipe G. Gozon, written in simple, easy-to-read English, launched at the author's 75th birthday. CJ met Henry, as friends fondly call him, more than three decades ago when both were actively practicing law; fully convinced of his 'proven competence, integrity, probity and independence,' CJ asked him several times in the late 1990s to consider joining SC, but he humbly declined, citing a commitment to develop TV-radio as the prime embodiment of the freedom of expression to transform society. CJ's earlier tribute, quoted on book pages 237-238, says in part: 'It is difficult to define Henry in one word, but I think Gutsy with a capital G as in Gozon comes closest.' (2) 'Stirred, Not Shaken' by Eduardo H. Yap -- CJ's foreword characterizes Eddie's '6Gs': gift of gab (both written and verbal), gift of giving (of himself and his possessions to favorite charities), and gift of genius (manifested in his persona and writings). (3) 'Echoes of God's Love' by Fr. Roberto B. Manansala -- a collection of concise, life-touching, unforgettable homilies for one whole liturgical year (Cycle B). CJ has run out of space for other notable events -- the lovely Christmas musicale at the home of Ave and Helen Cruz, the solemn affiliation of Titoy Pardo to the De La Salle Brotherhood, the 50th wedding anniversary of Louie and Triccie Sison, the 90th birthday of national artist F. Sionil Jose, etc. But let's not ever forget, the birth of our Lord Jesus Christ is the real reason for the joyous season.
